title: Mock QCM / Data modeling & SCD
summary: Synthetic QCM set for exercising AtlasNote question, attempt and review flows.
provenance: Original synthetic mock content created for AtlasNote UI testing. No private data, credentials or third-party content.

questions.prompt: What does an SCD Type 2 dimension preserve?

options.text: Historical versions of a dimension row.
options.explanation: Type 2 keeps previous states with validity metadata.

questions.explanation: Type 2 represents change over time with multiple versions.
questions.followUp: Which columns would you add for validity tracking?

questions.prompt: What should a fact table's grain statement describe?

options.explanation: Grain is the semantic unit of each row.
Technology does not define business grain.

questions.explanation: A precise grain prevents ambiguous joins and measures.
questions.followUp: Give a grain statement for an order-line fact table.

questions.prompt: Why use surrogate keys in a Type 2 dimension?

options.text: Different historical versions of the same business entity need distinct dimension rows.
options.explanation: The business key remains shared across versions.

options.text: They make every natural key unnecessary in source systems.
options.explanation: Sources still need their own identifiers.

questions.explanation: Surrogate keys allow facts to reference the correct historical dimension version.
questions.followUp: When should the fact lookup use event time?

questions.prompt: A KPI changes after joining a dimension. What should you inspect first?

options.text: Join cardinality and the grain of both sides.
options.explanation: Unexpected fan-out is a common cause.
Visualization does not alter row counts.

questions.explanation: Measure changes after a join often indicate cardinality or filtering effects.
questions.followUp: How would you prove the join is many-to-one?
